expected_evidence: Ice-core sulfate/sulfur-isotope spikes (e.g., Greenland GISP2/GRIP, Antarctic cores) dated to ~12,900 cal BP that would indicate a large explosive eruption coincident with YD onset
Tephra/volcanic glass shard layers in lake and marine sediments across multiple continents, geochemically fingerprinted to a known or unknown eruptive source
Sedimentary charcoal and soot/PAH records showing biomass-burning spikes that could be attributed to volcanic-triggered climate stress rather than an extraterrestrial impact winter

Reduced or reinterpreted extraterrestrial proxy signals (platinum, iridium, nanodiamonds, magnetic microspherules) at the YD boundary layer that the volcanic hypothesis would need to explain away or co-opt
Cosmogenic/geochemical dating (varve counts, ice-layer counting) tying any eruption horizon precisely to the onset of YD cooling (~-10900 to -10700 interval)

Comparative volcanological literature/model_prior reasoning about known Late Glacial eruptions (e.g., large Northern Hemisphere volcanic events) capable of producing a multi-year impact winter and continental-scale biomass burning
response.rationale: The hypothesis sits squarely in the 'younger-dryas' period bucket (interval -11000 to -10001 matches the YD onset), for which geological (0.65) and material (0.35) detectability are moderate-to-good — polar ice cores, varved lake sediments, and marine cores from this interval are extensively sampled and well-preserved, and tephra/sulfate/charcoal signals at the YD boundary have in fact been actively searched for and published on (this is a live, ongoing scientific controversy versus the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis). Astronomical-dating-adjacent proxies (ice-layer counting, 0.7) are also strong for this period, aiding precise chronological placement of any eruption relative to the cooling onset. Genetic (0.3) and oral_tradition/iconographic/linguistic/textual evidence are essentially inapplicable or non-existent this far back (textual = 0.0), so their absence carries no evidentiary weight against the hypothesis. Given moderate-to-good detectability for the most relevant kinds (geological, material), an absence of a clear, dated, multi-continent volcanic signal coincident with YD onset would be a genuinely informative negative result rather than an artifact of poor preservation — hence I do not fully discount findings either way. I weighted the adjustment toward the geological/material/astronomical mean (~0.55) rather than dragging it down with the near-zero textual/linguistic/oral scores, since those simply aren't expected evidence types for this hypothesis. Note: my characterization of the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis debate and its counter-volcanic explanations reflects model-prior knowledge of the scientific literature, not verified evidence text provided in this session, and should be treated as low-tier/unverified within this pipeline.
